# References {#sec-references}

## Standards and taxonomies

- Balaji, V. (2006). *A standard description of grids used in Earth system
  models.* GFDL/NOAA. The "logically rectangular" and mosaic framework.
  https://extranet.gfdl.noaa.gov/~vb/gridstd/
- ESMF Reference Manual, grid section: uniform, rectilinear and curvilinear
  as subtypes of logically rectangular. https://earthsystemmodeling.org
- CF Conventions, section 5 (coordinate systems) and the grid mapping
  appendix. https://cfconventions.org
- Weinkauf, T. (KTH, 2015). *Grids and interpolation* (lecture notes): the
  implicit, semi-implicit and explicit storage framing.
- Campbell, J. W., Blaisdell, J. M. and Darzi, M. (1995). *Level-3 SeaWiFS
  data products: spatial and temporal binning algorithms.* NASA Technical
  Memorandum 104566, Vol. 32.
- NASA OBPG. *Integerized Sinusoidal Binning Scheme for Level 3 Data.*
  https://oceancolor.gsfc.nasa.gov/resources/docs/format/l3bins/
  (archived copy: https://web.archive.org/web/20260106075308/https://oceancolor.gsfc.nasa.gov/resources/docs/format/l3bins/)
- Thompson, J. F., Soni, B. K. and Weatherill, N. P. (eds) (1998).
  *Handbook of Grid Generation.* CRC Press. Structured grids as a mapping
  from a uniform computational space to physical space.
- Wikipedia. *Regular grid.* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_grid
  (read 15 October 2026). Discussed in @sec-mis-wikipedia.
- GeoTIFF specification: tiepoints, pixel scale, PixelIsArea and
  PixelIsPoint.
